deepdive.sec: Microfinance / NBFC-MFI — rural JLG unsecured lending, post-stress recovery cycle

bull_bear.body:
- **Rights issue completion:** *"The balance rights issue money of INR200 crores, INR100 crores from the promoter and the balance INR100 crores from others who participated is expected this quarter, before the end of this quarter."* (The partly-paid line `SSFLPP`/BSE 890221 on the covering letter corroborates a rights issue in flight.)
- **Capital adequacy:** stated only qualitatively — *"Liquidity and capital adequacy are areas wherein at this point in time, we are holding good."* No CRAR number was given on the call.
- **Liquidity to be optimised down, not held:** *"As the situation is improving, as the environment is improving, we will like to optimize on the overall liquidity that we will carry in the balance sheet"* — tempered by *"in microfinance, it's always better to stay liquid than keep gasping for that."*
- **Under-provisioning is a known, deliberately deferred capital decision.** Stage-1 coverage at 40 bps vs peers ≥1%; MD accepts the gap and points at the trade-off — frontline officers are absorbed by the 90-plus pool — committing only to *"raise at least the bar to 50% in the 1 to 30 segment."* Timing framed by the analyst as *"maybe not this year, maybe next year"* and not contradicted.
- **Growth is to be funded without opex build:** *"The growth that we are going to get is with very limited or no investments on increasing from a cost side."*
- No buyback, dividend or M&A discussed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **El Nino / weak monsoon** — the single most-probed risk on the call. MD: *"El Nino, much spoken about what's going to happen, time alone will say. But proactively, the credit and business have worked together a strategy how to deal with new customers who are not exposed to any form of credit who are staying in a rented premise… So we put some game plan for select districts and states that are likely to be impacted. So it's a wait and watch with adequate controls."* July-to-date read: *"Thus far, in line with what we have seen in the balance month of this year… thus far, no adverse observation in the collection efficiency"* and *"as of now, we are not seeing any adversity in the way the portfolio is behaving."*
2. **Earnings quality depends on a wasting asset.** PPOP INR16cr ex-recoveries vs INR40cr with; the INR2,500cr 90-plus pool is explicitly terminal — *"This is the last year we're going to focus on the so-called 90-plus book because after that, we don't have expect customers who are 2 years or more thereafter paying us."* Clarified: *"the older 90-plus, we will not collect it… of course, you will have some 90 plus this year also. The older pool will stop starting next year onwards."*
3. **Stage-1 coverage at 40 bps vs peer ≥1%** — a real future P&L charge if flows normalise upward before coverage is rebuilt.
4. **New-book delinquency inching up** — flagged by an analyst (*"there is a slight inch up in the new book delinquency"*); management answered with the 99.5% CE aim rather than a normalised-delinquency number.
5. **Cyclicality / boom-bust history** — asked head-on: *"From 2013 onwards, we have seen this 3, 4 times now that in an up cycle, we scale up to INR8,000 crores, INR10,000 crores of AUM. And then as the down cycle starts versus our peers, our consolidation is heavier."* Answer was doctrine, not mechanism: process/controls, discipline, calibrated growth — *"If you wish to grow at 100% and your systems don't support, you're going to fall."* Note the INR10,000cr March-'28 aspiration is the same magnitude as the prior peaks that preceded consolidations.
6. **LOS migration execution** across 1,250 branches in Oct–Dec 2026 — collections and origination both ride on it.
7. **Sponsor-exit overhang** — MD would not answer how long Kedaara stays: *"if your question is aimed at saying that how long will Kedaara stay invested, no answers. But at least I see them here for at least next 2, 3 years."*
8. **Attrition / people risk** named as a top-3 priority: *"we are able to work on the attrition front and ensure that we retain people because over time, we realize that once the people are there on board, their productivity improves, reliability improves."*
9. **Customer retention against competition** for seasoned borrowers: *"Are we allowing those customers to go to competition or we are able to retain them"*; *"the good customers who have been with us… we don't lose them any cost."*
10. **Rights-issue money not yet received** — INR200cr is expected, not banked, as of the call.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- **Tone: relieved but consciously anti-triumphal.** Opening: *"it is a new morning for Spandana and a morning filled with hope"* — immediately self-checked: *"overall business is looking good, but that should not lead to complacency. So we are putting our head down to ensure that we stay focused on basics."* Closing is the same note: *"put our heads down and do our basics right, no heroics."*
- **Credible on disclosure.** The CFO volunteered PPOP on both bases (with and without recoveries) instead of only the flattering one; the MD accepted the Stage-1 coverage criticism outright (*"It's a very valid observation"*); and both refused to give an FY27 ROA number rather than manufacture one.
- **Precision under follow-up.** When an analyst inferred recoveries would be negligible from the written-off zone, the MD corrected him immediately (*"No, we are collecting from that only"*) and the CFO tightened the number in real time (INR300 crores "last year" → *"INR326 crores in last 18 months"*). Similarly the MD volunteered a self-correction on his own "last year" 90-plus statement without being pushed.
- **Answered a question nobody asked** — the SRO/multi-lender discipline point — which is a tell of management wanting the guardrail data on the record: *"one of the questions, of course, not asked, let me answer that."*
- **Governance framing:** unusually direct that the sponsor is hands-off on strategy (*"Kedaara has no role to play, what to grow, which markets to grow"*) while supportive operationally (monthly reviews, AI help offered).
- Watch-item on tone: growth ambition (INR10,000cr by Mar-'28, roughly a doubling) sits awkwardly beside the "calibrated growth" doctrine — management is aware, but the reconciliation was rhetorical rather than quantified.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
1. **The credit-cost guidance is a floor, not a ceiling, and management said so twice in different units.** Gross credit cost stays guided at 2.5–3% even though Q1 printed 2.1% *and* the transcript's own parenthetical says net credit cost was **negative** in Q1. Read together, that means the guide embeds an expected deterioration in the new book — the recoveries are what makes the net number ("Closer to 2%") look benign.
2. **Yield is at the end of its runway before NIM is.** With disbursal yield ~25.25% and book yield already 24.6%, essentially all remaining margin expansion must come from the liability side — which makes the CGS sanction pipeline and PSU-bank entry the actual FY27 margin story, not pricing.
3. **The "last year of 90-plus" statement is a dated earnings cliff, not a colour comment.** ~INR24cr of the quarter's INR51cr recovery was from the written-off pool; management guides INR150–200cr for FY27 and then stops. Anyone extrapolating FY27 PPOP into FY28 must strip that out — and FY28 is precisely the year the 3.5% RoA promise is parked in.
4. **Spandana + 3 at 3.7% (from 20–25%) is the strongest sector-wide datapoint on the call** — it says the SRO guardrails are binding in practice, which matters more for peers' loss-given-default than for Spandana's growth.
5. **The branch doctrine flipped without fanfare.** After a multi-quarter rundown, the network is now a floor (1,250) with a *revival* task-force for the worst 100 branches instead of closure — a deliberate rejection of the standard MFI consolidation playbook, justified as *"merger or closure in microfinance rarely leads to success."*
6. **The Individual Loan pilot's real significance is the eNACH rail, not the product.** It is the first Spandana product with a non-cash, non-centre-meeting repayment mechanism, and it is designed to migrate to new-to-Spandana borrowers with external track records — i.e. a template for growth that does not depend on JLG density.
7. **Opex falling ~11% in absolute rupees while AUM is guided up ~25%** is the least-discussed lever on the call (INR760-odd cr → ~INR675 cr), and management explicitly ties the growth to *"very limited or no investments on increasing from a cost side"* — operating leverage, not margin, may be where FY27 RoA improvement actually comes from.
8. **Two under-penetrated states carry the entire multi-year AUM ambition.** Tamil Nadu at INR16cr against a INR38,000cr industry and Maharashtra at INR288cr against INR24,000cr — the Mar-'28 INR10,000cr goal is implicitly a bet on these two, run by a CBO who *"has recently joined us."*
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position remains heavy: CRAR ~33.8% consolidated at Jun-26 (28.6% standalone), down from 40.8% / 36.9% at Jun-25 as the book re-levered; consolidated gearing 2.0x at Jun-26 versus 1.9x at Jun-25.
- Deck footnotes an undrawn equity call option: "Right to call up Rs 200 Cr out of the Rs 400 Cr partly-paid rights issue till March 2027".
- Liquidity of Rs 1,316 Cr as of 30-Jun-26 with incremental funding of Rs 1,597 Cr in Q1FY27; consolidated net-worth Rs 2,140 Cr (standalone Rs 2,208 Cr).
- Borrowing mix diversified with 47% of outstanding loans from banks at Jun-26 (NBFC 31%, Capital Markets 21%, FPI 1%), against 51% / 17% / 27% / 4% at Jun-25.
- Positive ALM on a cumulative basis with assets maturing faster than liabilities; average residual maturity of assets 10.3 months versus borrowings 8.8 months at Jun-26 (10.1 vs 10.2 at Mar-26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Geography is the operating segmentation.** Top states (as stated): Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra, Telangana, Odisha, West Bengal — *"about 60% of our total share"* (count stated inconsistently, see §2 call-out 5).
- **Under-penetrated states = the stated growth vector.** Tamil Nadu: *"our share currently is just about INR16 crores out of the industry of INR38,000 crores."* Maharashtra: *"we are at about INR288 crores as against the industry of INR24,000 crores. So 1.1% share, we want to at least double it to 2% share."* (Share % is management's own arithmetic, quoted not computed.)
- **The 100-branch turnaround cohort:** *"We carved out 100 branches where there was scope for improvement, either on the business or collections of both. And we're trying to put a separate team to revive this because merger or closure in microfinance rarely leads to success."*
- **Criss Financial (group company)** — the Individual Loan product is intended to roll into it: *"We want to make it a success and roll it pan India and for our group company, Criss Financial as well."*
- **Branch count is now stable-to-up, ending the rundown:** *"We have 1,250-odd branches (Standalone), and it will remain so. No further plans to merge down… In fact, it might actually go up if you really expand in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra."*
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Funding access held through the stress window** — the durable asset here is lender relationships, and management evidenced it rather than asserted it: *"even during trying times, institutions were quite supportive of Spandana for a variety of reasons, including the promoter caliber and credibility in the marketplace."* Corroborating number: bank share 44% → 47%, incremental cost 11.3%, INR1,597 crores raised in one quarter with only INR200 crores of that CGS-supported.
- **Sole-lender origination discipline** — the sharpest competitive datapoint on the call: *"today, as I talk to you, Spandana + 3 is about 3.7% only, which used to be about 20%, 25%. So 98% of the customers that I added were regular and we were the only borrowers at that point in time when we gave the loan."*
- **Density in six core states** with a branch network management refuses to shrink further (1,250 branches, revival-over-closure doctrine) — the stated reason being that in microfinance the network *is* the collection mechanism: *"merger or closure in microfinance rarely leads to success."*
- **Sponsor stability without operational interference:** *"Kedaara has no role to play, what to grow, which markets to grow, how to grow… everything is done by the management"* — with a stated horizon, *"at least I see them here for at least next 2, 3 years."*

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Framed as "Continuing on growth path with improving asset quality and profitability" with a "Turnaround visible across parameters" — Q1FY27 PAT of Rs 12 Cr versus a Q1FY26 loss, GNPA & NNPA of 3.6% & 0.7% at Jun-26 versus 3.8% & 0.7% at Mar-26 (consolidated).
- Loan book has been substantially reconstituted: "Portfolio originated under new credit rules constitute 91% of microfinance AUM" and 99.2% of that new portfolio is current; the new book (standalone, disbursed since 1 April 2025) grew from 188 to 4,058 Rs Cr between Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 while the old book ran down from 4,245 to 397 Rs Cr.
- Underwriting discipline shown through borrower quality at disbursement: 75% of customers had a maximum of +1 lender relationship (39% Unique / 36% Spandana+1 / 25% Spandana+2), ~98% were current at disbursement (98.3% current, 1.7% 1-30 dpd) and ~90% had loans with <Rs 1 L household outstanding (64% <50k, 26% 50k-1L, 9% 1L-1.5L, 1% 1.5L-2L).
- Lender overlap of Spandana+>=3 borrowers reduced to 3.7% at Jun-26 from 18.2% at Jul-25, with Unique customers rising to 36.6% from 27.9% over the same window.
- Well-diversified geography: ~52% of AUM from top 4 states and top-5 states at 59% of AUM; largest district is 2.3% of AUM and largest branch 0.3%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rating] Rating outlook changed to BBB+/Stable from BBB+/Negative by ICRA Ratings; CRISIL, CARE and ICRA now all at BBB+/Stable for bank facilities/NCDs (CARE CPs at A2), while India Ratings remains BBB+/Negative.
- [Subsidiary] Criss Financial Ltd (CFL) is a separately-rated group entity — ICRA and India Ratings both at BBB / Watch Positive — and is reported separately in branch, customer and headcount charts; overall collection efficiency is noted to include CFL IL and LAP portfolio.
- [Regulation] The "new credit rules" regime is the pivot of the disclosure: loans originated under new credit rules constitute 91% of MFI AUM, and the deck tracks the old book's runoff separately from the new book.
- [Provisioning] Consolidated PCR at ~81% (Stage 3 coverage 81.2%; standalone 80.8%), with total ECL provision of Rs 174 Cr on Rs 4,636 Cr of consolidated loans outstanding (3.7% coverage).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- **The NIM rebuild is two-sided.** Yield 22.8% → **24.6%** (mix + lower 90+ interest reversals, *not* repricing); overall borrowing cost 13.2% → **12.8%**, marginal 12% → **11.3%**. Result: NIM 9.9% → **12.5%**.
- **Headroom is nearly used up on the asset side:** *"our ideal yield at which we disburse is around 25.25%. So accordingly, we are very close to that number… yield going forward should see marginal improvement."* Remaining margin expansion has to come from liabilities.
- **CGS is the cheap-money wedge** (~10% or a little over) but is deliberately not the whole story — management pointed out non-CGS borrowing also priced well, to rebut the idea that the 11.3% is scheme-dependent.
- **Opex is being taken down in absolute terms:** ~INR760-odd crores (FY26) → ~INR675 crores (FY27E), *"we'll be in the same range in terms of the absolute number"* — while still funding Tamil Nadu/Maharashtra entry and automation: *"the savings that come through are plowed back in one form or the other."*
- **CFO's own framing of the margin agenda:** *"Our financial borrowing cost got elevated during the stress period. The focus is how do we bring that cost down and protect the NIMs as we progress."*
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** First Spandana note in the corpus — no prior quarter to diff against internally. Sequential deltas as management stated them: AUM +11% QoQ to INR4,887cr (prior quarter +12%); PAT INR12cr vs INR5cr; NIM 12.5% vs 9.9%; yield 24.6% vs 22.8%; GNPA 3.6% vs 3.8%; "Consolidated NPA" 0.68% vs 0.73%; 1-to-90 1.2% vs 1.3% of AUM; annualized credit cost 2.1% vs 3.2%; marginal cost of borrowing 11.3% vs 12%; overall cost of borrowing 12.8% vs 13.2%; bank share 47% vs 44%; new-vintage book 91%. Trigger set: rights-issue INR200cr balance (Q2 FY27, High), Perfios LOS migration (UAT end-Q2, cut-over Oct–Dec 2026, Medium).
- _Q2 FY27 → check:_ (a) did the **INR200cr rights-issue balance** actually land before 30-Sep-2026? (b) new-vintage book share hit **95%**? (c) X-bucket CE held at **99.5%** through the monsoon — and did the El-Nino district plan get tested? (d) 90-plus recoveries tracking to INR150–200cr (run-rate INR16–18cr/month → INR20cr target)? (e) marginal cost of borrowing below 11.3%, more CGS sanctions drawn, PSU banks actually onboarded? (f) LOS **UAT completed on time** — any slip in the Oct–Dec cut-over? (g) Individual Loan 8-branch MP pilot verdict after its stated 3-month test; (h) Stage-1 coverage moved off 40 bps? (i) branch adds in Tamil Nadu / Maharashtra started? (j) reconcile the marginal-cost basis (70 bps vs 120 bps) and the CGS sanction figure (INR545cr vs INR500cr) against the next disclosure.

outlook.body:
- **Disbursements FY27:** *"we are looking at anywhere between INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores."*
- **AUM exit FY27:** *"This year, we are aiming for about exit of about anywhere a little upwards of INR6,000 crores."*
- **AUM March FY28:** *"broadly, we are looking at a INR10,000 crores or thereabouts by March '28"* — explicitly soft: *"March '28, may turn out to be a guidance, which we will plan as we get into August, September times."*
- **Credit cost FY27 — TWO measures, both given:** gross *"2.5% to 3%"* re-affirmed (*"Very much. We are at, as I said, 2.1% for Q1 and the efforts are on to retain that"*); **net**, including recoveries — MD: *"Closer to 2%."*
- **90-plus recoveries FY27:** *"we are going to collect anywhere between INR150 crores to INR200 crores. We are trying to see if we can collect a little more than INR200 crores as well."* And the shelf-life warning: *"This is the last year we're going to focus on the so-called 90-plus book."*
- **RoA:** current 1%; *"3.5% kind of ROA is something that should be feasible"* — **FY28**, re-confirmed (*"This ROA of 3.5% was for FY '28, right, next year?" → "That's right."*). FY27 = *"should see more improvement in this number"* (no number given).
- **Yield:** *"our ideal yield at which we disburse is around 25.25%… yield going forward should see marginal improvement. But yes, then it should sustain from there."* No further rate hikes: *"there are no further plans to increase the rates at this point in time."*
- **Cost of borrowing:** *"we should see some further improvement in the coming quarter"*, driven by more CGS sanctions + PSU-bank entry.
- **Opex:** FY27 ~INR675 crores (vs FY26 ~INR760-odd crores); FY28 +10%.
- **New-vintage book share:** *"we should move to 95% or so in the coming quarter."*
- **Capital:** balance rights-issue **INR200 crores** *"expected this quarter, before the end of this quarter"* — see §9 and the trigger box.
- **Systems:** new LOS *"should be in the UAT stage by the end of this quarter. And October to December, we are going to be migrating, which is Perfios platform from Jayam."*

| 2 | Core **LOS platform migration** — Perfios replacing Jayam across the entire 1,250-branch network; UAT gate falls inside Q2 FY27, cut-over immediately after | **UAT by end-Q2 FY27; migration Oct–Dec 2026** | Commissioning | **Medium** | *"we are working on the new LOS platform, which should be in the UAT stage by the end of this quarter. And October to December, we are going to be migrating, which is Perfios platform from Jayam… That's a big initiative for the company, migrating 1,250 branches."* |

> **Excluded as triggers (dated but sub-threshold on impact vs own size):** the Individual Loan pilot — *"ready to be piloted in 8 branches in Madhya Pradesh… Over the next 3 months, we want to test it out"* — because management itself caps it: *"it cannot be a huge share."* Also excluded: further CGS sanctions ("sanctions are still coming") — no hard date.

outlook.body:
Not applicable in the order-book sense — the lender-equivalent pipeline is disbursement capacity and sanctioned-but-undrawn liability lines:
- **Funding pipeline:** INR1,597 crores drawn in Q1 of which only ~INR200 crores was CGS; MD/CFO stress the *undrawn* balance — *"INR500 crores sanctioned thus far, utilized is INR200 crores"* (and INR545 crores of CGS sanction cited in the opening), *"The rest is yet to be drawn. That clearly depicts that there is borrowings, which is available outside CGS as well."*
- **CGS pricing:** *"Pricing is just about at 10% or a little over 10% because there are sub-10%, there are marginally over 10% as well."*
- **New lender pipeline:** *"some of the names, banking names who are not part of the funding thus far are also talking to us"*; *"as days pass by, you will have PSU banks participating, which should also bring down the cost of acquisition."*
- **Explicit answer that liabilities are not the growth constraint** — asked directly whether *"access to liabilities can impede our growth targets this year"*, CFO's reply pointed to the non-CGS drawdown at 11.3% as evidence it will not.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Individual Loan product (the one genuinely new product line):** *"Individual loan product is ready to be piloted in 8 branches in Madhya Pradesh. So we are putting about 8 -10 people. Over the next 3 months, we want to test it out because this is a completely different product, better underwritten with eNACH facility."* Existing customers first, then *"new to Spandana customers as well, anyone who's got a track record elsewhere."* Management sets expectations low on size but high on quality: *"it cannot be a huge share, but definitely a much better underwritten offering."*
- **Tamil Nadu + Maharashtra expansion** — new branches this year, backed by the newly-filled South CBO seat: *"We have a new Chief Business Officer for South… He is going to take care of Andhra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala"*, completing all four regional CBOs (North/South/East/West).
- **Collections tech as a margin lever:** telecalling with dynamic QR — *"we are able to receive INR30-odd lakh from customers directly online through the QR code that we generate when we are calling the delinquent customers. So we are trying to see whether we can increase that INR30 lakhs to INR50 lakhs"*; plus outsourced bot-calling — *"the bots can call you repeatedly without really talking about 80 connects a day."*
- **Perfios LOS** carries embedded credit + collections modules: *"That also has its own inbuilt credit platform, collections platform that will lead to a lot of insights into how we approach customers… skip trace of customer mobile numbers."*
- **Sponsor-side AI optionality:** *"If there are any AI initiatives since they have that skill and expertise, they [Kedaara] are willing to help us on AI-led initiatives."*
